thread:
Nora Alvarez: Weird dashboard alert: overall p50 dropped 30ms but p95 jumped 400ms for /v1/embed when we flipped routing to favor variant-b. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/latency?endpoint=embed
Tom Becker: saw that too. Per-variant panels show variant-a p95=120ms, variant-b p95=780ms, but overall p95=780ms and p50=48ms which seems off given variant weights (variant-a ~90% traffic).
Isha Rao: can you paste the raw backend breakdown? UI might be merging tdigest rollups incorrectly across route tags.
Nora Alvarez: raw query:
```
SELECT caller_variant, tdigest_percentile(0.5, tdigest) AS p50, tdigest_percentile(0.95, tdigest) AS p95, sum(sample_count) as samples
FROM telemetry.latency
WHERE endpoint='embed' AND time > now() - interval '15m'
GROUP BY caller_variant;
```
Nora Alvarez: results: variant-a p50=50ms p95=110ms samples=900; variant-b p50=40ms p95=780ms samples=10.
Tom Becker: Huh, variant-b has only 10 samples but huge tail, shouldn't move overall p95 that much if we compute p95 from merged tdigest. Is the console merging per-variant histograms and then computing pctls naively by re-binning?
Isha Rao: Our documented merge mode: we can either merge tdigest sketches server-side into a composite tdigest then compute percentiles, or the UI can convert per-variant sketches to fixed buckets and merge. The latter will overweight sparse, high-outlier buckets due to rounding.
ConsoleOps Bot: deploy-rollout:route_weight_change variant-b increased to 10% for rollout/2023-11-01-10:13
Nora Alvarez: But rollout event shows 10% weight for variant-b; still math says overall p95 should be near 120ms. Something's wrong with weight accounting when merging bucketed histograms: UI appears to be normalizing each variant histogram to 1000-sample equivalence before merging.
Tom Becker: can we reproduce by forcing UI to use server-merged tdigest vs client-merged buckets? I toggled "merge-mode=server" and overall p95 immediately dropped to 130ms.
Isha Rao: That proves it. UI bucket-merge is normalizing counts incorrectly (probably dividing by max bin count or using percent-of-panel instead of absolute sample weights).
Nora Alvarez: Impact: alerting uses overall p95 displayed value; we triggered an incident page because alert threshold was based on UI value. Need to avoid UI-driven numeric alerts.
Tom Becker: Short-term mitigation: change alerts to read server-merged percentiles only (endpoint:aggregate:merge=server). Also add a low-sample guard: if any subgroup has <50 samples, show a warning icon and don't let that subgroup dominate numeric merges.
Isha Rao: Long-term: fix client merge algorithm: merge tdigest sketches (we can ship a lightweight tdigest.js) or fetch server-merged sketch via telemetry API. Also update docs about when UI histogram merges are purely visual.
Nora Alvarez: I'll file ENGPLAT-3330 with repro steps, screenshots, and the toggle that caused the console to show inconsistent p95. Assign @Isha to lead the fix.
Isha Rao: taking it. Plan: 1) change alert queries to prefer server pctl, 2) fix UI to label merged-mode as visual-only, 3) ship tdigest merge lib. ETA for bullet 1: 2h.
deploy-bot: alerting-config:updated by rollout/2023-11-01-12 (alerts now reference telemetry.aggregate_mode=server)
Tom Becker: Thanks. Also can we add 'sample_weight' breakdown to the endpoint detail panel so it's obvious when a single low-sample variant could influence numbers?
Nora Alvarez: good idea. I'll add to the ticket.
Isha Rao: quick note for postmortem: alerting pipeline should always derive thresholds from server-side aggregates; UI numbers are for humans and can be flaky with sparse cohorts.
Nora Alvarez: closing loop: once the change is live, I'll re-run historical alerts and confirm no false positives. :thumbsup:
